Question: What is your earliest childhood memory?
Answer: Domestic Violence ahead. I loved Gulab Jamun in my childhood. I hate them now. Reason? I was nearly six y/o then. I woke up in the middle of the night and started shouting ‘Gulab Jamun’ ‘Gulab Jamun’. Everyone was sleeping. Papa. Maa. And Didi. Maa woke up. She convinced me that she'll make it tomorrow. ‘Just sleep for now,’ she said. ‘Papa has a morning shift.’ I didn't listen to her. I started crying. I started saying ‘Gulab Jamun’ even louder. Maa got angry. She beated the shit out of me. My dad, my lovely dad can't see me in pain. Ever. So he woke up as soon as he sensed Maa was using domestic violence against me. Papa got angry. Super angry. He asked my mom to go and make the Gulab Jamun right now as I was crying like a just-born infant. Maa said I'll make it tomorrow. You have a morning shift and cooking will create much noise. No one will be able to sleep. Maa gave me one last slap so that I won't repeat such havoc again. Papa got angry at Maa. He said ‘don’t hit him like that’. Hit him like ‘this’. And ‘this’. He made me a punching bag. He then threw me out of bed and while I was in the air, I was thinking is it a WWE Royal Rumble match that Papa wants to eliminate me? Didi was watching this domestic violence from the washroom. The door was slightly open. And, of course, I never asked for a Gulab Jamun to anyone ever again. Be it Mom. Dad. Or even a shopkeeper. P.S. I want to make a cute baby like him someday. But, at the same time, I don't want to get married. Dear Ronaldo, please guide me. We are all gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are things you shouldn’t do in life?
Answer: Yesterday was my friend's birthday. I texted him on WhatsApp and asked him to meet me in the evening. I called and he asked me where we could meet: 'Our chai point,' I said. 'Are you sure? We can go somewhere else as well.’ 'That's fine. Let's just sit there and talk.’ We met there in the evening. I already had my coffee and it was paid. He came with his cup of tea and we sat there and talked for more than an hour. Just we two. I told him I didn't want a party. I said I just texted you at midnight as everybody would've been calling you, as well, and it's so frustrating receiving the calls all day. ‘Exactly,' he said. 'Everyone calls you on your birthday and wants to talk to you for long. And, they ask the same thing. It's so tiring.’ 'I know that,' I said and started laughing. 'I think I should start switching off my phone on my birthdays just like you. And the party, omg, everyone is asking for a party.’ ‘I think it should be the total opposite. The person having the birthday should receive the party so that he would get excited about his birthday getting nearer.’ 'What a philosophy. Let's start it from today.' he laughed. He didn't want a party as well. We sat there as if it was a normal day. We talked about adulting, marriage, jobs, and travelling. We also gossiped about our college's girls. That's how birthdays should be like. Normal. P.S. DO NOT ASK FOR A PARTY ON BIRTHDAYS. INSTEAD, GIVE IT. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Do you like to receive gifts?
Answer: Depends. Yesterday, I received a gift. I love 5-star. I love that Fruit Barfi. I love cold-coffee (not this one). And I love Cocacola for one good reason, we can mix it with other things. XD But, when I received this, my first reaction was why did it come? I asked the delivery guy and he told me the sender's name. I said I know. I called her. 'You should save money for better things,' I said and started giving her the reasons why this was a pretty bad idea. I kept roasting and she was laughing. 'I'm making fun of these things as I don't want you to repeat this mistake again,' I joked. 'And… how many times do I tell you that whenever you gift something, it should be a book? You could've gifted me two books in that amount.’ She knew. She was searching for a book but it was really hard to find a book that I haven't read or that was already not on my shelf. I listened to her. The reason was genuine. And when she was about to cut down the call, I said a feeble thank you. ‘Finally,' she said. 'I will eat these things and they will be gone. If you gift me a book, it stays. You get such low thankyous if you gift things other than books.’ I replied. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are the advantages of being lonely?
Answer: It's a lovely feeling. I was talking to an old man who had a tea shop in Nainital. His shop was always occupied. But one day, while I was sightseeing, alone, it started raining heavily. I parked my rented Ntorq and went to the stall. I asked for a coffee. And since there was no one there, except me, that old man started talking to me. 'So, where did you come from?’ he asked. 'MP. I live in Madhya Pradesh.’ I said. ‘And you're with?’ 'Myself. I came for the solo travel.’ I said. 'That's great, beta,' he replied. 'At least you're enjoying yourself, alone, other than the youngsters who take sleeping pills or take anti-depressants when they feel lonely.’ 'Haha, thank you, uncle. To be honest, I also feel alone and lonely and depressed. But it's just that, these days, loneliness has become an addiction. It brings joy to me.’ 'You enjoying being lonely?’ 'Sort of, uncle.’ I said. 'I like the feeling where you feel extremely low and melancholic but you choose to discover yourself instead of taking the pills to sleep. You choose to turn that loneliness into solitude. For me, reading helps like magic.’ 'My son hates books. He never studies though he has all the perks he can have.’ 'I hated books, too, while I was in school. I started loving them once I needed them. XD.’ I replied while sipping the last bit of coffee. The rain had stopped while we were busy talking. Or, I was busy talking. I gave him a hanger-wide smile. And went more up, on the mountains. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What is the brutal truth about people?
Answer: Love isn't eternal, always. Someone might say they can't live without you. Your fragrance might've done magic to her. You might be the only person she wanted to touch. But a few years down the line, she could be found holding hands in public. And that person would not possibly be you. That's not a dark fiction story. It's there. It keeps happening to people all the time. Your ex might be happily married to someone else. And you'll slowly start becoming a stranger to her. Love stories can be hurt stories. It starts with people being strangers and it can end up with them being a stranger again. How ironic, isn't it? We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Is there something you are scared of doing?
Answer: No strings attached. One-night stand. Hookup. No matter how amusing it sounds to me, I wonder if I can ever do it. I have reached an age where people I know have started doing it. They tell me about their experiences and sometimes, I think it might be fun. Except, it won't be, for me. I know myself. And I know what'll happen to me if I do it rathly. No strings attached are for people who've lost faith in love. I have. No strings attached are for people who're emotionally drained. I am. No strings attached are for people who can't imagine being with someone in the future. I can't. Despite that, I know that it will be a grave idea. I may throw away my body to someone, someday, but the very next day, I'll dread it. How can you undo a human touch even if it lasted for an hour? How can you get rid of the fragrance that's still lingering from your sweatshirt? How can you forget someone whose breath was mixing with your breath? Whose heartbeats were dancing alongside your heartbeats. Whose body was engulfed by your body while they were quivering. How can you? How can you lose contact with that person and not long for her anymore? I wonder. I just wonder and think of the consequences which might follow if I don't fall for anytime soon! We all are gifted, Shubham KP
